title: Solo Tokyo in Sakura Season
subtitle: 4 days of cherry blossoms, ramen counters & neon-lit nights for one
description: You're arriving in Tokyo at the exact moment the city transforms. Late March is when the first sakura burst open — Shinjuku Gyoen's 1,000 trees, the lantern-lit canal at Meguro River, the moat at Chidorigafuchi turning pink. This itinerary is built for solo travelers: counter-seat ramen shops, standing sushi bars, sprawling temple grounds to wander alone, and neighborhoods like Shimokitazawa and Yanaka where the pace slows down. Tokyo is one of the world's great solo cities — everything is designed for a party of one.
highlights: Cherry blossoms at Shinjuku Gyoen — 70+ varieties, 1,000 trees
Chidorigafuchi moat boat ride under sakura canopy
Tsukemen at Fuunji — Tokyo's best dipping ramen
Senso-ji Temple at dawn — Asakusa without the crowds
Shimokitazawa vintage shops and craft coffee
Meguro River cherry blossoms lit by paper lanterns at night

essentials.title: 🌸 Cherry Blossom Timing
essentials.text: Late March is early bloom season in Tokyo — March 20-23 falls right at first bloom (typically March 22-26). You'll catch the magical transition from buds to first petals. Shinjuku Gyoen has early-blooming varieties that peak before Somei Yoshino. Check real-time sakura forecasts on japan-guide.com.

essentials.title: 🚇 Getting Around
essentials.text: Get a 72-hour Tokyo Metro pass (¥1,500/~$10) or use a Suica/Pasmo IC card — tap-on, works on all trains, buses, and convenience stores. Google Maps transit directions are flawless in Tokyo. Trains run 5am–midnight. For late nights, taxi or walk — Tokyo is extremely safe at any hour.

essentials.title: 🍜 Solo Dining Culture
essentials.text: Tokyo is the world capital of solo dining. Counter seats at ramen shops, conveyor belt sushi (kaitenzushi), standing bars (tachinomi), and ticket-machine restaurants are all designed for one. No awkwardness, no judgment — eating alone is completely normal. Ichiran has private booths with curtains.

essentials.title: 💴 Money and Tipping
essentials.text: Japan is increasingly cashless (IC cards, PayPay QR), but carry ¥10,000-20,000 cash for small shops, shrines, and market stalls. Tipping is NOT customary — the price is the price. Convenience stores (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart) have international ATMs and excellent food.

days.title: Shinjuku — Gardens, Neon & Late-Night Ramen
days.description: Start in the heart of Tokyo's biggest district. Morning in the serene gardens of Shinjuku Gyoen chasing early cherry blossoms, afternoon exploring the labyrinthine streets around the station, evening diving into Kabukicho's electric nightlife — all within walking distance.

activities.title: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
activities.description: Tokyo's finest cherry blossom garden — 58 hectares with over 1,000 trees across 70+ varieties, including early-blooming kanzan and shidarezakura (weeping cherry). Arrive at opening to have the grounds nearly to yourself. The Japanese Traditional Garden section, sakura reflecting in the pond, is the most photogenic spot in the city.
details: 🌸 ¥500 entry · Opens 9:00am · No alcohol allowed (keeps it peaceful)
📸 Best spots: Japanese Garden pond reflection, English Landscape lawn, Taiwan Pavilion
🚶 Give yourself 2+ hours — vast and every corner has something
🎒 Bag check at entrance — no tripods or large bags inside

meals.name: Konbini Coffee and Onigiri
meals.description: Start the day the Tokyo way — hot canned coffee and a salmon onigiri from any 7-Eleven near Shinjuku Station. Japanese convenience store food is legitimately excellent. Try the egg sandwich (tamago sando) too.

tips.text: Shinjuku Gyoen opens at 9am sharp. Be in line by 8:50 — the first 30 minutes are magical before tour groups arrive. Use the Shinjuku Gate entrance, closest to the station.

activities.title: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane)
activities.description: A narrow strip of tiny yakitori stalls behind Shinjuku Station's west exit, here since the post-war era. Each stall seats 6-8 people at smoky counters. Order chicken skewers and a draft beer, watch the grill master work — old Tokyo at its finest.
details: 🏮 Each stall seats 6-8, perfect for solo counter dining
🍢 Must-try: negima (chicken and leek), tsukune (meatball), kawa (crispy skin)
💰 Cash only at most stalls

activities.title: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory
activities.description: Free observation deck on the 45th floor with panoramic views of Tokyo — on clear days you can see Mt. Fuji. No ticket needed, just go through security and take the elevator up. One of Tokyo's best free attractions.
details: 🆓 Free entry · Open until 11pm (South Tower)
🗻 Best Mt. Fuji views: clear mornings or just before sunset
📍 5 min walk from Shinjuku Station west exit

meals.name: Fuunji
meals.description: One of Tokyo's most legendary tsukemen (dipping ramen) shops. Thick, rich fish-and-pork broth with perfectly chewy noodles. Solo counter seats, ticket machine ordering. Expect a 20-30 min queue but it moves fast.
meals.meta: 💰 $ · 📍 Yoyogi, 5 min south of Shinjuku Station · Counter seats only

activities.title: Kabukicho and Golden Gai
activities.description: Tokyo's most famous nightlife district. Kabukicho is neon-drenched — Godzilla on the Toho building, pachinko parlors, arcades. Then Golden Gai: six narrow alleys, 200+ tiny bars seating 5-10 each. Many welcome solo travelers; this is where you make friends over whisky.
details: 🍺 Golden Gai — most bars charge ¥500-1000 cover + drinks from ¥700
📸 Kabukicho neon looks best just after dark (6:30-7:30pm)
🚫 Some bars are regulars-only — look for 'Tourists Welcome' signs
🎮 Solo karaoke (hitokara) — private rooms from ¥500/30min nearby

meals.name: Omoide Yokocho Yakitori Round 2
meals.description: Return to Memory Lane for dinner — it transforms at night when lanterns glow and smoke billows between the alleys. Pick any stall, sit at the counter, charcoal-grilled chicken with cold Asahi.
meals.meta: 💰 $$ · 📍 Omoide Yokocho, Shinjuku west exit · Cash only

tips.text: Golden Gai is best around 8-9pm. Bars are tiny — if one's full or feels unwelcoming, try next door. There are 200+ options. Many bartenders speak some English.

days.title: Old Tokyo — Temples, Markets and Otaku Culture
days.description: A journey through time. Dawn at the 7th-century Senso-ji Temple, morning in nostalgic Yanaka, afternoon cherry blossoms at Ueno Park, and evening in Akihabara's electric wonderland. East Tokyo is where tradition and obsession collide.

activities.title: Senso-ji Temple at Dawn
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest temple (founded 645 AD) is a tourist madhouse by 10am — but at 6:30am, you'll have the Thunder Gate, massive red lantern, and incense-filled main hall to yourself. Nakamise shopping street is shuttered and atmospheric. Walk slowly and watch the monks begin morning rituals.
details: ⛩️ Grounds open 24h · Main hall opens 6:00-6:30am (seasonal)
📸 Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon) — iconic red lantern, zero crowds at dawn
🎋 Draw an omikuji fortune (¥100) — bad luck? Tie it to the rack
🏮 Five-story pagoda area has the best morning light

activities.title: Yanaka Ginza and Yanaka Cemetery
activities.description: Yanaka survived the WWII firebombing and feels like 1950s Tokyo. Yanaka Ginza is a retro shopping street with street food, cat statues, and zero chain stores. The adjacent cemetery has a stunning cherry blossom tunnel — a canopy of sakura lines the main path.
details: 🐱 Tokyo's 'cat town' — real cats and cat-themed shops everywhere
🌸 Yanaka Cemetery sakura tunnel — most peaceful blossom spot in Tokyo
🍡 Try menchi-katsu (fried meat croquette) and taiyaki from street stalls
📍 Nippori Station → 3 min walk to Yanaka Ginza

meals.name: Pelican Cafe
meals.description: Near Asakusa — legendary bakery making Japan's most famous shokupan (milk bread) since 1942. The cafe next door serves thick-cut toast, eggs, and coffee. Simple, perfect, solo-friendly counter.
meals.meta: 💰 $ · 📍 Taito, near Asakusa · Opens 8:00am · Counter seating

tips.text: From Senso-ji, take the Yamanote Line from Uguisudani to Nippori for Yanaka. 15 minutes and feels like teleporting to a different era of Tokyo.

activities.title: Ueno Park Cherry Blossoms
activities.description: Japan's most famous hanami (flower-viewing) park — over 1,000 cherry trees line the main avenue, and during bloom season the path becomes a pink tunnel with families picnicking underneath. Grab a konbini bento and sit under the trees like a local.
details: 🌸 The main cherry tree avenue is the classic hanami scene in Tokyo
🏛️ Tokyo National Museum — Japan's oldest and largest museum (¥1,000)
🦢 Shinobazu Pond — rent a swan boat for a solo cruise
🍱 Konbini bento + Strong Zero under sakura = peak Tokyo experience

activities.title: Ameyoko Market
activities.description: Bustling open-air market running under the Yamanote Line tracks from Ueno to Okachimachi. Fresh seafood, dried fruits, sneakers, chocolate strawberries — Southeast Asian energy in central Tokyo.
details: 🦐 Fresh uni (sea urchin), crab legs, grilled scallops on sticks
🍫 Chocolate strawberry stalls near the Okachimachi end
💰 Cash preferred at most stalls

meals.name: Sansada Tempura
meals.description: Operating since 1837, this Asakusa institution serves crispy, light tempura at the counter. Watch each piece fried to order. The tendon (tempura rice bowl) is about ¥1,500 and legendary.

activities.title: Akihabara Electric Town
activities.description: Ancient temples to anime paradise in one subway ride. Multi-story arcades, manga shops, retro game stores, and electronics outlets. Even non-otaku love the sensory overload. Try the vintage game floors at Super Potato.
details: 🎮 Super Potato — 5 floors of retro games, playable consoles on top floor
📦 Mandarake — massive secondhand manga and collectibles
🕹️ Arcades — crane games, rhythm games, purikura photo booths
📍 Best experienced after dark when all the neon comes alive

meals.name: Kanda Yabu Soba
meals.description: One of Tokyo's three great soba restaurants, established 1880. Hand-cut buckwheat noodles served cold on bamboo with dipping sauce. Minimalist, meditative, perfect for solo dinner. The building is a beautiful traditional wooden structure.

tips.text: For solo conveyor belt sushi, try Sushiro or Kura Sushi — order from a tablet, sushi arrives on a mini train. No interaction needed, no awkwardness. Brilliant concept.

days.title: West Side — Vintage, Vinyl and River Blossoms
days.description: The creative, youthful side of Tokyo. Morning at Meiji Shrine and Harajuku, afternoon exploring Shimokitazawa's vintage shops and curry joints, evening along the Meguro River watching cherry blossoms glow under thousands of pink paper lanterns.

activities.title: Meiji Shrine (Meiji Jingu)
activities.description: Walk through the towering torii gate into 170 acres of old-growth forest right in central Tokyo. The approach through the forest feels like leaving the city entirely. Write a wish on an ema wooden plaque and hang it at the shrine.
details: ⛩️ Free entry · Opens at sunrise (~5:40am in March)
🌲 Forest planted in 1920 with 100,000 trees donated from across Japan
📸 The massive cypress torii gate on the main approach is the photo
🎋 Ema plaque (¥500) — write a wish, read other visitors' wishes too

activities.title: Harajuku and Takeshita Street
activities.description: Step from ancient forest into Tokyo's youth fashion capital. Takeshita Street is a narrow packed lane of crepe shops and kawaii fashion. Cat Street (one block over) is the cooler, less crowded version with independent boutiques and cafes.
details: 🍦 Giant cotton candy and crepes — Harajuku's street food signatures
👗 Cat Street for independent Japanese fashion brands
☕ % Arabica Coffee on Cat Street — minimalist espresso perfection

meals.name: Bills Omotesando
meals.description: Australian cafe famous for its ricotta hotcakes — fluffy, pillowy pancakes practically mandatory in Tokyo. Solo counter seats overlooking the kitchen.

activities.title: Shimokitazawa
activities.description: Tokyo's most beloved bohemian neighborhood — a tangle of narrow streets packed with vintage clothing shops, record stores, tiny curry restaurants, and live music venues. Feels like a village inside a megacity. Perfect for aimless solo wandering.
details: 👕 Vintage shops: Flamingo, Stick Out, New York Joe Exchange
🍛 Shimokitazawa is curry town — try Curry Spice Gelateria
🎵 Check for afternoon live shows at Shelter or Club Que
☕ Bear Pond Espresso — legendary (and famously intense) barista

meals.name: Curry Spice Gelateria
meals.description: A Shimokitazawa original — artisanal curry with rotating spice-infused gelatos for dessert. Counter seats, solo-perfect.

tips.text: Shimokitazawa is 3 stops from Shibuya on the Keio-Inokashira line. South side has more vintage shops, north side more food. Just wander — best discoveries are unplanned.

activities.title: Meguro River Cherry Blossoms at Night
activities.description: The 4km stretch of Meguro River from Nakameguro to Meguro is lined with 800+ cherry trees. During bloom season, thousands of pink paper lanterns illuminate the petals — their reflections ripple in the water below. Walk the entire length slowly, stopping at the small bars and wine stands set up along the banks.
details: 🏮 Lantern illumination daily through early April, dusk to 9pm
🍷 Pop-up wine and champagne stands along the riverbank
📍 Start at Nakameguro Station and walk south toward Meguro
📸 The bridge near Nakameguro Station is the most photographed spot

activities.title: Shibuya Crossing
activities.description: No Tokyo trip is complete without crossing the world's busiest intersection. Watch from the Starbucks 2F for the aerial view, then cross with the crowd. Find the Hachiko statue at the north exit.
details: 📸 Best views: Starbucks 2F or Mag's Park rooftop (free)
🐕 Hachiko statue — the world's most loyal dog, north exit
🌃 Most impressive after dark with all the screens lit

meals.name: Afuri Ramen Nakameguro
meals.description: Light, refreshing yuzu shio (citrus salt) ramen — clear golden broth with a yuzu punch, completely different from heavy tonkotsu. Modern counter-seat-only restaurant. Perfect after a sakura walk.
meals.meta: 💰 $$ · 📍 Nakameguro · Counter seats · Ticket machine ordering

days.title: Imperial Sakura, Tsukiji and Ginza Farewell
days.description: Your final day is Tokyo at its most refined. Morning at Chidorigafuchi — the Imperial Palace moat becomes a tunnel of cherry blossoms, best seen from a rowboat. Fresh sushi at the outer Tsukiji Market. Afternoon in elegant Ginza, evening under the illuminated weeping cherry at Rikugien Garden.

activities.title: Chidorigafuchi Cherry Blossoms and Boat Ride
activities.description: The most iconic sakura scene in all of Tokyo — 260 cherry trees arch over the Imperial Palace moat, their branches forming a pink tunnel reflected in the green water below. Rent a rowboat and drift under the canopy. Arrive early — boat queues build fast during peak bloom.
details: 🚣 Boat rental: ¥800/30min · Opens 9:30am during sakura season
🌸 The walkway along the moat is equally beautiful without a boat
📸 Best light: morning sun illuminating blossoms against the moat
🏯 Kitanomaru Park is adjacent — free, peaceful, cherry trees throughout

activities.title: Tsukiji Outer Market Breakfast
activities.description: The inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains a wonderland of fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), and street food. Grab sushi at any counter — all source from the same market. Fresh tuna at 7am hits different.
details: 🐟 Tuna, uni, scallop — all incredibly fresh from overnight auction
🥚 Tamagoyaki (sweet egg) on a stick — the Tsukiji signature street snack
📍 10 min walk from Tsukiji Station or 15 min from Chidorigafuchi by taxi

meals.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Sushi Counter
meals.description: Pick any of the sushi counters in the outer market — Sushi Dai, Daiwa Sushi, or just follow the queue. Fresh nigiri for breakfast is a quintessential Tokyo experience.
meals.meta: 💰 $$-$$$ · 📍 Tsukiji Outer Market · From 5am · Counter seats

tips.text: March 23 is a Monday — Imperial Palace East Gardens close on Mondays and Fridays. Spend time at the Chidorigafuchi walkway and Kitanomaru Park (both open) instead.

activities.title: Ginza Shopping District
activities.description: Tokyo's most elegant neighborhood — wide boulevards, department stores, art galleries, and Japanese craft shops. Visit Ginza Six (rooftop garden with views), Itoya stationery store (12 floors of Japanese paper and pens), and the architectural showcase along Chuo-dori.
details: 🛍️ Ginza Six — luxury department store with a stunning rooftop garden
✒️ Itoya — 12 floors of stationery heaven, perfect for gifts home
🍵 Higashiya Ginza — traditional Japanese sweets with matcha
📍 Ginza is walkable from Tsukiji (15 min) or one subway stop

meals.name: Ginza Kagari
meals.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand chicken paitan (white broth) ramen in Ginza. Creamy, golden chicken broth unlike any ramen you've had. Tiny shop
